title: What is self-directed learning?
message: Self-directed learning is a process in which learners take the initiative to identify learning needs, set goals, choose resources and strategies, and evaluate outcomes.

comparison.label: 1. Identify a goal
comparison.text: What do I need to learn, and what do I want to achieve?

comparison.label: 2. Choose a path
comparison.text: Which resources, people and strategies will help me learn?

comparison.label: 3. Evaluate progress
comparison.text: What have I learned, and what should I change? Self-assessment helps here.

result: “I need to distinguish training from inference. I will use the chapter and a concept map, then check whether I can explain the difference.”
decision: Teachers and peers can support the process; the learner takes responsibility for the choices.

title: What is self-assessment?
message: Self-assessment means judging your own work and learning against explicit criteria, then using that judgment to improve.

comparison.label: 1. Check the criteria
comparison.text: What should I be able to explain or do?

comparison.label: 2. Look for evidence
comparison.text: What can I demonstrate? Where do I still struggle?

comparison.label: 3. Choose a next step
comparison.text: What will I revise, practise or check again?

result: “I can explain what a token is, but I still confuse training and inference. I will revise that link in my map and explain it again.”
decision: AI can offer feedback; the learner checks the evidence and decides what to improve.

Training vs. Inference — Explained Simply

Imagine a language model as a student who has already studied for an exam.
